g9-history-uh7-t7.overview: Egalitarian System of Governance sits inside States, Principalities, Population Movements and Interactions in Ethiopia, 13th to mid-16th Century. Population movements, states, and principalities in Ethiopia open Unit 7 of Grade 9 History in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it studies the “Solomonic” dynasty and the Christian kingdom after 1270. Then it surveys the Muslim principalities along the Zeila trade route. Next, it follows the war between the Christian kingdom and the Sultanate of Adal. Also, it looks at the southern and central states and the great Oromo expansion. Finally, it explains the Gadaa system and the egalitarian rule of Sidama, Gedeo, and Konso. Students will also learn how these population movements shaped modern Ethiopia today.
objectives: Outline the factors behind the restoration of the “Solomonic” dynasty.
Explain the population movements of the 16th century in Ethiopia.
Analyse the relationship between the Christian kingdom and Muslim sultanates.
Describe the Oromo Gadaa system and its values.
Compare the egalitarian rule of the Sidama, Gedeo, and Konso.
